### [`v4.10.4`](https://github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/releases/tag/v4.10.4): Preserves segment position across alternatives

[Compare Source](https://github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/compare/v4.10.3...v4.10.4)

Fixes patterns like `x{**/a,b}` which *should* be treated like `x*/a` and `xb` because the doublestar appears mid-pattern.

#### What's Changed

- fix: preserve segment position across brace alternatives by [@​yuefdev](https://github.com/yuefdev) in [#​125](https://github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/pull/125)

#### New Contributors

</details>

##### Notable Changes

##### Potential changes to macOS Universal Binary availability

With Apple and its ecosystem progressively dropping support for Intel-based
architectures, it has become apparent that the Node.js project may not be able
to maintain the universal binaries we currently distribute for the full lifetime
of Node.js 26. This change serves to communicate that risk. At present, our
intention remains to continue shipping universal binaries supporting both Apple
Silicon and Intel-based Macs for as long as practical.

Contributed by Antoine du Hamel in [#​63055](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/63055).

[Compare Source](https://github.com/nodejs/node/compare/v26.0.0...v26.1.0)

##### Notable Changes

##### Experimental `node:ffi` module

Node.js now includes an experimental `node:ffi` module for loading dynamic
libraries and calling native symbols from JavaScript.

The API is gated behind the `--experimental-ffi` flag and, when the Permission
Model is enabled, requires `--allow-ffi`.

This API is inherently unsafe. Invalid pointers, incorrect signatures, or accessing memory
after it has been freed can crash the process or corrupt memory.

Contributed by Paolo Insogna in [#​62072](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/62072).

### [`v26.0.0`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v26.0.0): 2026-05-05, Version 26.0.0 (Current), @​RafaelGSS

[Compare Source](https://github.com/nodejs/node/compare/v24.22.2...v26.0.0)

We're excited to announce the release of Node.js 26! Highlights include the Temporal API enabled by default,
updates to the V8 JavaScript engine to 14.6, Undici to 8.0, and several important deprecations and removals
as we continue to modernize the platform.

As a reminder, Node.js 26 will enter long-term support (LTS) in October, but until then, it will be the "Current" release for the next six months.
We encourage you to explore the new features and benefits offered by this latest release and evaluate their potential impact on your applications.

##### Notable Changes

##### Temporal API

The Temporal API is now enabled by default in Node.js 26. Temporal is a modern date/time API for JavaScript
that provides a more robust and feature-rich alternative to the legacy `Date` object.

Contributed by Richard Lau in [#​61806](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/61806).

##### V8 14.6

The V8 engine is updated to version 14.6.202.33, which is part of Chromium 134.

This version also includes:

- Upsert (<https://github.com/tc39/proposal-upsert>): `[Weak]Map.prototype.getOrInsert()`, `[Weak]Map.prototype.getOrInsertComputed()`
- Iterator sequencing (<https://github.com/tc39/proposal-iterator-sequencing>): `Iterator.concat()`

Contributed by Michaël Zasso in [#​61898](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/61898).

##### Undici 8

Undici has been updated to version 8.0.2, bringing new features and improvements to Node.js's HTTP client implementation.

##### Deprecations and Removals

- \[[`dff46c07c3`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/dff46c07c3)] - **(SEMVER-MAJOR)** **crypto**: move DEP0182 to End-of-Life (Tobias Nießen) [#​61084](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/61084)
- \[[`93c25815ee`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/93c25815ee)] - **(SEMVER-MAJOR)** **http**: move writeHeader to end-of-life (Sebastian Beltran) [#​60635](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/60635)

`http.Server.prototype.writeHeader()` is now fully removed. Use `http.Server.prototype.writeHead()` instead.

- \[[`c755b0113c`](https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/c755b0113c)] - **(SEMVER-MAJOR)** **stream**: move \_stream\_\* to end-of-life (Sebastian Beltran) [#​60657](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/60657)

The legacy `_stream_wrap`, `_stream_readable`, `_stream_writable`, `_stream_duplex`, `_stream_transform`, and `_stream_passthrough` modules are now fully removed.

pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.16.1`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.1): pnpm 12.16.1 [Compare Source](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.16.0...v12.16.1) This release fixes `pnpm install` hanging on a cold store in workspaces that install Cargo crates, and `pnpm pack` shipping a file that `files` excludes by name. ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer hangs on a cold store in a workspace that also installs Cargo crates or a Rust toolchain. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now apply a `files` entry that names a file after the glob and directory entries, as npm does. A file excluded by name, such as `!dist/index.js`, stays out even when a later `dist/**` matches it. A file named by its path, such as `lib/secret.js`, ships even when a later `!lib/*.js` matches it. - `pnpm install` no longer leaves a broken symlink in an injected workspace dependency when the package links to a file outside its published files and pnpm imports by hardlink. Installing a git dependency now skips internal directory symlinks when importing its files into the store. - `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm rebuild` now refresh privately hoisted `.bin` shims in `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/.bin` after a dependency build replaces a script target with a native executable [#​17402](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17402). - `pnpm install` now reads a package's manifest to decide its peer dependencies when it updates an existing lockfile, as it does when it resolves from scratch. - Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222). - pnpm now accepts the `--cache-dir ` flag, as in `pnpm install --cache-dir /tmp/pnpm-cache` [#​17422](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17422). - When the version or range given to `pnpm unpublish` matches every published version, the error now says so and shows the same command with `--force`. Before, the error suggested running `pnpm unpublish @`, the command that had just failed. #### Platinum Sponsors
#### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.16.0`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.16.0): pnpm 12.16 [Compare Source](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.15.0...v12.16.0) This release adds a global `--env-file` flag, updates to a symlinked `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and `pnpm setup --no-modify-path`. It also fixes two security issues, in zstd decompression and in signing. ##### Minor Changes - Added a repeatable global `--env-file ` flag to load environment variables from dotenv-style files before running a command. Later files override earlier files, variables already in the environment are preserved, and loaded variables are visible to user-level `.npmrc` interpolation and lifecycle scripts [#​7111](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7111). - pnpm can now update a `pnpm-lock.yaml` that is a symlink. List the directories the lockfile may link into in the `symlinkedLockfileTargetDirs` setting, in the global config or with `PNPM_CONFIG_SYMLINKED_LOCKFILE_TARGET_DIRS`. pnpm writes the update to the file the symlink points to if that file is inside one of these directories. The symlink stays in place. pnpm ignores this setting in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` [#​17222](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17222). - Added a `--no-modify-path` option to `pnpm setup`. It installs pnpm without adding it to `PATH`, leaving the shell config file, the Windows registry, and the GitHub Actions environment files unchanged. `pnpm setup` then prints the lines to add yourself [get.pnpm.io#37](https://github.com/pnpm/get.pnpm.io/issues/37). ##### Patch Changes ##### Security - Fixed memory exposure and allocation handling vulnerabilities when processing zstd-compressed data [#​17388](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Signing in pnpm and pnpr no longer uses arithmetic that may leak the private key through timing. This covers shared artifacts, OCI registry tokens, and OIDC login state [advisory](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0387). ##### Installing packages - A dependency symlink that pnpm cannot point at the wanted target now fails the install with an error that names the link. This happens when the filesystem still serves the old link after pnpm removed it, as a `node_modules` served by a virtual filesystem does. pnpm used to remove the link again without end and crashed with a segmentation fault once the thread ran out of stack. - Concurrent workspace installs no longer lose store-index rows when initializing the shared SQLite index [#​17388](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17388). - Agent skill links now keep the same target across installs when a package version is installed with several sets of peer dependencies. An install no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_AGENT_SKILL_PATH_OCCUPIED` on a skill link that pnpm created for another of those copies [#​17319](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17319). - pnpm now fails at once, without retrying, when a downloaded package archive contains a rejected entry path [#​17205](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17205). - pnpm now builds a git-hosted dependency in every new location it links the dependency into, such as a new global virtual store slot or a fresh `node_modules`. When the side-effects cache holds the build output, pnpm restores it from there. Before, only the install that fetched the dependency built it. This also fixes dependencies that are already in the store [#​17224](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17224). - Changes a `preResolution` hook makes to the lockfiles now take effect. The hook now also runs when pnpm installs from an up-to-date lockfile. An error thrown by the hook now fails the install. - A custom fetcher in the pnpmfile can now call `fetchers.directory` to fetch a package from a local directory. The call rejects with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` if the lockfile pins an archive integrity for the package. Previously, calling `fetchers.directory` failed with a `TypeError`. - `packageImportMethod: copy` now also applies to packages that have lifecycle scripts or patches. On a filesystem that supports block cloning, such as ReFS or a Dev Drive on Windows, these packages were cloned [#​17195](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17195). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `autoInstallPeers: false`, a package that workspace projects use with different peer versions is now installed once per peer variant, so each project's copy resolves that project's peer [#​17395](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17395). - Under `nodeLinker: hoisted`, `pnpm install` now leaves a patched package that is already in place alone. The same holds for a package whose peers include a patched package, such as every package peering on a patched `react-native` [#​17188](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17188). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, an install that stops partway no longer leaves the next install trusting the packages it was replacing. Before, reverting the change that started the stopped install, such as a patch edit, kept the half-replaced package in `node_modules`. ##### Repeat installs and changed settings - A repeat `pnpm install` now acts on a change to these settings. Before, it reported "Already up to date". - `storeDir` or `virtualStoreDir`: it recreates `node_modules`. - `globalVirtualStoreDir`: it links the packages from the new directory. - `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`: it renames the virtual store directories. - `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` turned on: it runs the builds it skipped. - `trustLockfile` turned off: it verifies the lockfile. - `pnpm add`, `pnpm remove`, and `pnpm update` now fail if `node_modules` does not match the current settings. Run `pnpm install` to recreate it. Previously, these commands removed and reinstalled `node_modules` without asking. They report: - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE` if `node_modules` was linked from a different store. - `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_VIRTUAL_STORE` if it was linked from a different virtual store directory. - `ERR_PNPM_MODULES_BREAKING_CHANGE` if it was installed by an incompatible pnpm version, or if `node_modules/.modules.yaml` cannot be read. - `ERR_PNPM_NODE_LINKER_DIFF` if it was installed with a different `nodeLinker`. `pnpm update` now also fails with `ERR_PNPM_HOIST_PATTERN_DIFF` and the other errors `pnpm add` reports for a changed hoist pattern or `virtualStoreDirMaxLength`. - An install filtered to some workspace projects now fails if `node_modules` was installed with a different `nodeLinker`, `hoistPattern`, `publicHoistPattern`, store, or virtual store. Before, it recreated `node_modules` and left the projects it skipped without their dependencies. A `pnpm install` of the whole workspace still recreates `node_modules` [pnpm/tasks#217](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/217). - `pnpm install` and the `verifyDepsBeforeRun` check now notice an edited patch file when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. - `pnpm install` now takes its fast path in a workspace with `patchedDependencies` when the previous install ran with another major version of pnpm. - `pnpm install` now relinks the bins of a workspace package when its `bin` field changes, including with `--frozen-lockfile` and an unchanged lockfile. A filtered install relinks them in the selected projects, and the next install that covers the remaining projects relinks them there [#​17324](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17324). - `pnpm install` now removes command shims from `node_modules/.bin` when a workspace dependency renames or removes an entry from its `bin` field [pnpm/tasks#211](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/211). ##### Resolving dependencies and the lockfile - A package that a plain range and a `:` specifier both resolve from one registry is now recorded once in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and installed once. The lockfile key names the registry a package resolved from. When that registry declares a prefix, through `prefix` in `registries` or through `namedRegistries`, the package is keyed `@:` however its dependency was written: with the prefix, as a plain range its scope routes to that registry, or through the default registry. Before, the plain range was keyed `@`, so one tarball was installed twice and `instanceof` checks and module singletons broke between the two copies. The same name and version served by two registries still get separate entries. When several prefixes declare one registry, its packages are keyed by the lexicographically smallest prefix. If a scope you route reaches a registry that also declares a prefix, your next `pnpm install` re-keys those entries, which shows up as a lockfile diff. Commit it. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` installs the lockfile as recorded. - `pnpm install` now resolves a scope's packages again when the scope is routed to another registry in `registries`. Before, the lockfile kept the versions and integrity resolved from the old registry, so the install failed when the new registry did not serve a locked version or served different content. pnpm records in the workspace state which registry each scope routed to, so a fresh clone without that record installs the lockfile as recorded. Changing the default registry resolves nothing again, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is unchanged. - When `autoDedupe` is off, a workspace project's dependencies now resolve from its own ranges, like they do with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Previously, another project's narrower range could hold them back. For example, `ajv: "*"` now resolves to the latest Ajv even if another project depends on `ajv@^6`. Packages that a project lists in `peerDependencies` still follow the versions other projects use. `pnpm dedupe` and installs with `autoDedupe: true` still pick one version that satisfies every range. Set `autoDedupe: true` if CI runs `pnpm dedupe --check` [#​17235](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17235). - An optional dependency written with a named-registry prefix, such as `work:^1.0.0`, now fails the install when it cannot be resolved but the lockfile already has a matching entry from that registry. Such a dependency was skipped, which removed its entries from the lockfile. - With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a `workspace:` dependency written as a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib-a`, in a workspace package now resolves from that package's directory [#​17284](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17284). - Fixed `pnpm install` failing with `ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` when a workspace package injected through a relative path, such as `workspace:../lib`, has `catalog:` dependencies. Their catalog entries now resolve the way they do for a package injected by name [#​17280](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17280). - `pnpm dedupe` now refreshes cached registry metadata while re-resolving locked versions [#​17208](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17208). - `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails when the only difference is a `deprecated` notice that the registry added or removed after the lockfile was written [#​17198](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17198). - Installs delegated to a pnpr server now resolve every prefix declared for a registry URL. A dependency or lockfile entry that used the second of two prefixes for the same registry, such as `zeta:` next to `work:` in `namedRegistries`, failed on the server [pnpm/tasks#204](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/204). - Registry revisions are now addressed at `/@+r` [pnpm/tasks#208](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/208). ##### Adding packages and global packages - `pnpm add @` and `pnpm add @` now install the version the tag or range resolves to, even when the saved range allows a newer one [#​17234](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17234). - `pnpm add ` without a version now installs the version under the dist-tag set by the `tag` setting. An `npm:` alias or a `jsr:` dependency without a version resolves that tag too. The setting is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global config, `PNPM_CONFIG_TAG`, and `--config.tag`, and defaults to `latest`. - `pnpm add` now accepts the lowercase short options `-p`, `-d`, `-o`, and `-e` as aliases of `--save-prod`, `--save-dev`, `--save-optional`, and `--save-exact`. - `pnpm -D install ` now saves the package to devDependencies. An `add` option such as `-D` or `-E` written before `install ` was rejected as an unexpected argument. - `pnpm add -T` now reports that the short option is ambiguous and points to `--save-types` and `--tilde`. - Global packages installed with `pnpm add -g` are now linked from the global virtual store, so global packages that share dependencies share one copy. Set `virtualStoreType: project` to give each global install its own virtual store. - `pnpm add -g` and the other `--global` commands now fail with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_VIRTUAL_STORE_DIR_WITH_GLOBAL` when `--virtual-store-dir` is passed. A custom `--hoist-pattern` fails with `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_HOIST_PATTERN_WITH_GLOBAL`. Passing `--link-workspace-packages`, `--shared-workspace-lockfile`, or `--config.lockfile-dir` with `--global` also fails, with the matching `ERR_PNPM_CONFIG_CONFLICT_*_WITH_GLOBAL` code. ##### Registries, proxies, and login - pnpm now reads the `strictSsl` and `localAddress` settings from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, the global `config.yaml`, `PNPM_CONFIG_*` environment variables, and `--config.*` options. This includes `pnpm self-update` and the download of the pnpm version pinned in `packageManager`. Before, pnpm read them only from `.npmrc` as `strict-ssl` and `local-address` and ignored the other sources [pnpm/tasks#201](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/201). - When Corepack runs pnpm and the native binary has to be downloaded, the download now uses the proxy from pnpm's config. That proxy comes from `PNPM_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY` and the matching variables, the global `config.yaml`, and the user `.npmrc`. Previously, the download read the proxy only from `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` [pnpm/tasks#215](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/215). - When the `pnpm` package downloads its native binary on first run, as it does under Corepack, it now trusts the CA certificates from the `ca`, `ca[]`, and `cafile` settings of `.npmrc`, including the ones scoped to the registry. A registry behind a private CA failed with `fetch failed` before, unless `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` named the CA. A project `.npmrc` is used only while the download is checked against npm's signature. Node.js versions that cannot add CA certificates after startup still need `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. - `pnpm login` saves the token in `/auth.ini` again. Since v12.1.0, an unscoped login had made its registry the default for every project that did not name a registry. A login now also removes the token an earlier login saved for that registry or scope under `_auth` in the global `config.yaml`. `pnpm login --scope` still routes the scope through the global `registries` setting. - pnpm no longer warns that a `registries` entry routed through the `@` scope matches no configured registry. pnpm applied such an entry and its options such as `serverType` while reporting it as ignored [pnpm/tasks#184](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/184). ##### Running scripts and other commands - `pnpm ci --lockfile` and `pnpm ci --config.lockfile=true` no longer delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `pnpm ci` now always keeps the lockfile and runs a frozen install from it. - `pnpm deploy --legacy` now checks the workspace lockfile against `minimumReleaseAge` and the other resolution policies, as `pnpm install` does, and fails with `ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION` when a locked version is too new. It used to deploy an older version that is not in the lockfile without a warning [#​17209](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17209). - `pnpm deploy` now keeps a deployed symlink to a directory inside the project even if the directory is not among the deployed files, such as a link into `node_modules` [#​17288](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17288). - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` now keep `pnpm.config` in the published `package.json`. They also always include the file `pnpm.config` points to in the tarball [#​17210](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/17210). - `pnpm -r publish --batch` now sends `PUT /-/pnpr/v0/publish`, the batch publish endpoint that pnpr serves. - `pnpm audit --ignore` and `pnpm audit --ignore-unfixable` now exit with a non-zero code when vulnerabilities at or above the audit level remain after ignoring. Before, these commands always exited with code 0. - `pnpm audit --fix` and `pnpm audit --interactive` now fail with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_FIX_WITH_IGNORE` when combined with `--ignore` or `--ignore-unfixable`.
